author: Ivan Ball-llovera
name: MMCA business module (five layers + tests + migrations)
description: A new business module for an existing MMCA solution: the Shared, Domain, Application, Infrastructure, and API projects, an aggregate root with invariants and domain events, the IModule registration, a REST controller, domain and application test projects, and a migrations project for the module's own database. Run it from your solution root.

app.description: The solution / root namespace this module belongs to, for example Contoso.Support.

aggregate.description: The module's aggregate root, singular PascalCase, for example Invoice.

aggregateLower.description: Lower-case aggregate name: local variables, route segments, and resource-string prose.

moduleLower.description: Lower-case module name: routes and the data-source key.

moduleUpper.description: Upper-case module name: the design-time connection-string environment variable.

appShortName.description: Last dotted segment of the app name, used by the design-time factory's database name.

appShortNameUpper.description: Upper-case short name: the design-time connection-string environment variable.

postActions.description: Wire the module into the solution.

manualInstructions.text:
dotnet new cannot make these edits for you. Until they are done the module is invisible to the host and to the fitness rules. Do them in order: steps 1 and 2 are what make it compile.

1. SOLUTION: add the eight new projects.
     dotnet sln <YourApp>.slnx add Source/Modules/<Module>/*/*.csproj Tests/Modules/<Module>/*/*.csproj Source/Hosting/<App>.Migrations.SqlServer.<Module>/*.csproj

2. PROJECT REFERENCES: nothing references the new projects yet, so their namespaces do not resolve.
   - <App>.Web.csproj: add a ProjectReference to <App>.<Module>.API and to <App>.Migrations.SqlServer.<Module>.
   - <App>.Architecture.Tests.csproj: add a ProjectReference to ALL FIVE layer projects (Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Shared, API). The map in step 4 names a type from each.

3. IDENTIFIER ALIAS: in Directory.Build.props, copy the existing <Compile Include ... Link> block and point it at Source/Modules/<Module>/<App>.<Module>.Shared/<App>.<Module>.GlobalUsings.IdentifierType.cs, with Condition="'$(MSBuildProjectName)' != '<App>.<Module>.Shared'". Without it the identifier alias is invisible outside its own project.

4. ARCHITECTURE MAP: add five lines to your *ArchitectureMap.cs, one per layer:
     Module("<Module>", Layer.Domain, typeof(<App>.<Module>.Domain.<Module>.<Aggregate>).Assembly),
     Module("<Module>", Layer.Application, typeof(<App>.<Module>.Application.ClassReference).Assembly),
     Module("<Module>", Layer.Infrastructure, typeof(<App>.<Module>.Infrastructure.AssemblyReference).Assembly),
     Module("<Module>", Layer.Shared, typeof(<App>.<Module>.Shared.<Module>.<Aggregate>DTO).Assembly),
     Module("<Module>", Layer.Api, typeof(<App>.<Module>.API.Controllers.<Module>Controller).Assembly),
   A module missing from the map is silently NOT covered by the layering and isolation rules.

5. HOST: register the module's error-code translations next to the existing ones in your Web host's Program.cs:
     services.AddErrorResources<<Module>ErrorResources>();
   ModuleLoader discovers the IModule itself, so there is nothing else to register.

6. MIGRATION: create the module's first migration.
     dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate --project Source/Hosting/<App>.Migrations.SqlServer.<Module> --startup-project Source/Hosting/<App>.Migrations.SqlServer.<Module> --context SQLServerDbContext
